Against it, no Tabular List instruction asks for it, and the 7th character already shows a fracture under routine follow-up. Defensible either way.

citations.S82.251E: ICD-10-CM Official Guidelines for Coding and Reporting FY2027, Section I.C.19.c.1: the open fracture designations in the 7th character for fractures of the forearm, femur and lower leg, including ankle, are based on the Gustilo open fracture classification, and when the Gustilo classification type is not specified for an open fracture, the 7th character for open fracture type I or II should be assigned; fractures are coded with the 7th character for subsequent care for encounters after the patient has completed active treatment and is receiving routine care during the healing or recovery phase. Section I.A.19: the assignment of a diagnosis code is based on the provider's diagnostic statement that the condition exists. Here the surgeon documents an open displaced comminuted fracture of the shaft of the right tibia that is healing as expected six weeks after fixation; the note describes the wound and its flap cover but names no open fracture type, so the 7th character for a subsequent encounter for open fracture type I or II with routine healing is assigned.
citations.W11.XXXD: ICD-10-CM Official Guidelines for Coding and Reporting FY2027, Section I.C.20.a.2: assign the external cause code, with the appropriate 7th character (initial encounter, subsequent encounter or sequela), for each encounter for which the injury or condition is being treated. Here the fracture followed a fall from a ladder and this is a subsequent encounter for it, so the fall is reported with the 7th character for a subsequent encounter.

coder_notes: A 12 cm wound with extensive skin and muscle damage that needed a muscle flap reads like a higher open fracture type, but the provider names none; classifying the wound is not the coder's call, and the guideline gives the default for exactly this case. The guidelines state that there is no national requirement to report external cause codes (Section I.C.20); this test set reports them where the note supports them. Place of occurrence, activity and external cause status are used only at the initial encounter and are not documented here. Aftercare Z codes are not used for injuries; the 7th character shows that this is a follow-up visit. The fibula was not broken. The aching in the leg is part of the healing fracture. Acetaminophen is taken as needed. In practice this documentation would lead to a provider query; the gold is what can be reported from the note as written.
